claim: A transformer layer under Megatron tensor parallelism requires exactly two all-reduces in the forward pass and two in the backward pass, i.e. four blocking communication operations per layer.
stance_target: the claim that tensor parallelism is ruled out by a PCIe Gen2 x4 fabric, because its per-layer communication count is fixed and cannot be reduced by tuning
scope_conditions: Megatron intra-layer model parallelism, column-parallel + row-parallel GEMM fusion, transformer block
quoted_support: This enables us to perform all GEMMs in a simple transformer layer using only two all-reduces in the forward path and two in the backward path (see Figure 4).

claim: The MLP block under Megatron TP needs only one all-reduce in the forward pass and one in the backward pass because the two GEMMs are fused column-parallel then row-parallel, eliminating an intermediate synchronization point.
stance_target: the minimum achievable TP communication per MLP block, which sets the floor for TP cost on any fabric
scope_conditions: MLP block, column-parallel first GEMM, row-parallel second GEMM
quoted_support: This approach splits both GEMMs in the MLP block across GPUs and requires only a single all-reduce operation in the forward pass (g operator) and a single all-reduce in the backward pass (f operator).

claim: Vocabulary-parallel output embedding adds an all-reduce after the input embedding and an all-gather for the output logits, on top of the per-layer TP collectives.
stance_target: the extra communication that embedding-heavy models pay under TP
scope_conditions: Transformer with weight-tied input/output embeddings, vocabulary parallelized across GPUs
quoted_support: Since each partition now only contains a portion of the embedding table, an all-reduce (g operator) is required after the input embedding. For the output embedding, one approach is to perform the parallel GEMM ... add an all-gather Y = all-gather([Y1, Y2])

claim: Megatron-LM trained an 8.3B-parameter GPT-2-like model on 512 V100-32GB GPUs at 15.1 PFLOPs sustained with 76% scaling efficiency.
stance_target: the reference point for what TP can achieve when NVLink-class bandwidth is available
scope_conditions: 512 Tesla V100 SXM3 32GB GPUs, 32 DGX-2H servers, 8-way model parallelism for the 8.3B model
quoted_support: We illustrate this approach by converging transformer based models up to 8.3 billion parameters using 512 GPUs. We sustain 15.1 PetaFLOPs across the entire application with 76% scaling efficiency when compared to a strong single GPU baseline that sustains 39 TeraFLOPs, which is 30% of peak FLOPs.

claim: Megatron's testbed provided 300 GB/s intra-server bandwidth via NVSwitch and 100 GB/s inter-server bandwidth via 8 InfiniBand adapters, the hierarchy TP was designed around.
stance_target: the claim that TP assumes a fast intra-node tier that a PCIe Gen2 x4 box does not have
scope_conditions: 32 DGX-2H servers, NVSwitch intra-node, 8 InfiniBand adapters per server
quoted_support: Our infrastructure is optimized for multi-node deep learning applications, with 300 GB/sec bandwidth between GPUs inside a server via NVSwitch and 100 GB/sec of interconnect bandwidth between servers using 8 InfiniBand adapters per server.

claim: An 8B-parameter model requires 8-way model parallelism in Megatron's configuration, while a 1.2B model fits on a single GPU.
stance_target: the model-size-to-parallelism-degree mapping that determines whether a 7B model needs TP at all
scope_conditions: V100-32GB, GPT-2-style architecture, hidden size per head 96
quoted_support: The configuration with 1.2 billion parameters fits on a single GPU whereas the 8 billion parameter model requires 8-way model parallelism (8 GPUs).

claim: Megatron's f and g operators are conjugates: f is identity in forward and all-reduce in backward, g is all-reduce in forward and identity in backward, so each TP boundary costs one collective per direction.
stance_target: the mechanism that fixes TP's communication count at two collectives per GEMM pair
quoted_support: f is an identity operator in the forward pass and all reduce in the backward pass while g is an all reduce in the forward pass and identity in the backward pass.

claim: TP collectives sit on the critical path between GEMMs, so unlike DDP's gradient all-reduce they cannot be fully hidden behind computation.
stance_target: the claim that TP's cost on a slow fabric is latency-exposed, not just bandwidth-limited
scope_conditions: Megatron intra-layer parallelism; all-reduce between column- and row-parallel GEMMs
quoted_support: The output of the second GEMM is then reduced across the GPUs before passing the output to the dropout layer.
